variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: AI governance and regulation engineering turns policy, risk tolerance, and legal advice into controls that a team can run and audit. It connects an AI system's purpose, affected people, model and data versions, evaluation evidence, human oversight, release decision, and production response.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Use NIST AI RMF as connected outcomes”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Govern
pairs.detail: Define risk tolerance, roles, escalation paths, inventory rules, review cadence, and retirement responsibilities.
pairs.explanation: Define risk tolerance, roles, escalation paths, inventory rules, review cadence, and retirement responsibilities.

pairs.label: Map
pairs.detail: Describe intended use, affected people, dependencies, foreseeable misuse, impacts, and assumptions.
pairs.explanation: Describe intended use, affected people, dependencies, foreseeable misuse, impacts, and assumptions.

pairs.label: Measure
pairs.detail: Evaluate risks and controls with quantitative and qualitative methods, uncertainty, slices, and independent review.
pairs.explanation: Evaluate risks and controls with quantitative and qualitative methods, uncertainty, slices, and independent review.

pairs.label: Manage
pairs.detail: Prioritize risks, choose treatment, constrain or stop deployment, monitor, recover, and communicate.
pairs.explanation: Prioritize risks, choose treatment, constrain or stop deployment, monitor, recover, and communicate.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is traceable accountability: every material decision must connect a system version and risk to an owner, evidence, control, decision, and follow-up action.

Map: Describe intended use, affected people, dependencies, foreseeable misuse, impacts, and assumptions. Measure: Evaluate risks and controls with quantitative and qualitative methods, uncertainty, slices, and independent review. Manage: Prioritize risks, choose treatment, constrain or stop deployment, monitor, recover, and communicate.

variants.prompt: What is the core invariant of an operational AI governance system?
options: Every material decision connects a system version and risk to an owner, evidence, control, decision, and follow-up action.
Every AI system uses the same control checklist.
A legal policy page exists before launch.
The model provider owns every downstream application risk.
variants.explanation: Traceable accountability lets a reviewer reconstruct what was assessed, who decided, which conditions applied, and what happened next.

variants.prompt: Why should EU AI Act dates and role mappings live in a maintained obligations catalog instead of application conditionals?
options: Because scope, guidance, and implementation schedules can change, while each decision must preserve the interpretation and source used at that time.
Because engineers never need to enforce controls.
Because every AI use case has identical duties.
Because legal interpretation eliminates the need for technical evidence.
variants.explanation: A maintained catalog can be reviewed and versioned without burying changing legal assumptions inside product code.

Approve if the dashboard has no incidents yet.
Delete the old evaluation so reviewers are not confused.

When a dashboard contains many charts.
When raw prompts are retained forever.
When only aggregate satisfaction is measured.
